precepts.text: Sit not at all with another man's wife; don't play with it. Don't be drinking around somebody else's wife, lest thine heart incline unto her, and through thy desire thou fall into destruction. Both of y'all are going to destroy everything.
precepts.point: Read on in Genesis 39: he end up going to prison behind this, because she lied on him.

note.label: Character & Integrity: The Hidden Strength Behind Wisdom

precepts.why:
“the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man.” His master saw that the Lord was with him and made him overseer over his house, and “the Lord blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake.” And “Joseph was a goodly person, and well favoured”: he had a very good reputation, and people looked at him as a man of integrity and good character.

Then his master’s wife “cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.” He refused: his master had committed all that he had to his hand, “neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?” Nobody was watching him. He could have done it, but he said no. That is where integrity comes from: making the right decision when nobody is watching.

Ecclesiasticus 9:9 gives the same wisdom as a command: “Sit not at all with another man’s wife, nor sit down with her in thine arms, and spend not thy money with her at the wine; lest thine heart incline unto her, and so through thy desire thou fall into destruction.” Do not sit with another man’s wife at all. Do not play with it. Do not be drinking around somebody else’s wife, because your heart will incline to her, and both of you will destroy everything.

Joseph lived that. When “there was none of the men of the house there within,” she caught him by his garment, “and he left his garment in her hand, and fled.” He knew it was wickedness that would destroy his reputation and everything he had worked so hard for, and that he would not only be sinning against her but against the Lord. He fled rather than sit with it, even though he went to prison when she lied on him.

That's what got David caught up: he did not look away, and it brought all the other problems that came with it.

note.label: Pay The Price: Pleasure Now Regret Later

precepts.why:
Sirach says “Turn away thine eye from a beautiful woman”, and it begins with the eyes. Your eyes are directly correlated with your mind; they work in sync, and what you see makes your mind react a certain way. When you see something inappropriate online, not even porn, which is obvious, but something you know is not right, and you find yourself clicking and looking, you are not in control. You are down that rabbit hole looking for that feel good, because sin feels good. It is enjoyable.

That is why Moses is set before us in Hebrews: “Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. The pleasure of sin is only for a season, and you are going to pay the price for it. There is a price that is going to be paid.

That little season we deem as pleasure is only pleasure because your mind has convinced you it is, and that is because you have made an agreement with your eyes to keep looking. That is what got David caught up. He did not look away, and it brought all the other problems that came along with it.

So the best thing to do is turn away. Turning your head is proof you have control of your members; that is called self-control. If you cannot turn away, Christ is not the captain of that ship; Satan is driving. “For many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman”, deceived because they looked and did not turn away, when a simple motion of the head could have saved them a world of problems. Moses chose affliction with the people of God over the pleasure; that is the choice set before us.

precepts.text: You cannot keep the law in your mouth while conversing with people who know nothing of it; talk with those who love the Lord and have wisdom.
precepts.point: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth: when you open your mouth, what comes out is supposed to be scriptural; your conversation has to be modeled after what this book says. When people leave this truth the Lord removes his words out of their mouth, and their whole conversation changes: nothing is left but slander, falsehood, strange doctrines, and flattering speech.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“Let thy talk be with the wise, and all thy communication in the law of the most High.” You cannot keep the law in your mouth while conversing with people who know nothing of it. Talk with those who love the Lord and have wisdom.

All thy communication in the law of the most High: that is “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth”. Keep company where the law is the talk, and the law stays in your mouth.

precepts.text: Do not gaze on a maid, because looking is looking to lust.
precepts.point: A man cannot take fire in his bosom and not be burned, nor go on hot coals and not be burned; so he that goes in to his neighbour's wife and touches her shall not be innocent.

note.label: Proverbs 6: The Surety, the Sluggard, and the Six Things the Most High Hates

precepts.why:
“Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” The heart is your mind, and the lust starts there, with the looking.

Ecclesiasticus says not to start: “Gaze not on a maid, that thou fall not by those things that are precious in her.” Do not gaze on a maid, because looking is looking to lust. The gaze is how she takes you with her eyelids, and the fall comes by those things that are precious in her.

By means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread, and the adulteress hunts for the precious life. It begins with the eyes, so keep them off her.

precepts.text: Let all our communication be in the law of the Most High, having all things in common.
precepts.point: Fear came on every soul, and all that believed were together and had all things common. Having all things common means the same speech and the same mind, perfectly joined together, with blameless conversation and pleasure in the law, so that when the mind is fixed on the law, materialistic things stop mattering.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“Let thy talk be with the wise, and all thy communication in the law of the most High.” All the communication in the law. That is what having all things in common looks like: the same speech and the same mind among the believers, perfectly joined together in the law.

With the mind fixed on the law, the possessions and goods stopped mattering, and they were parted to all men as every man had need.

points: You have to counsel about the issues you are dealing with, but there is somebody you should not be counseling with about these emotional issues: your wife. Be not jealous over the wife of thy bosom, and teach her not an evil lesson against thyself. That jealousy goes into resentment: you unloaded all your emotional issues on her, and now you get into an argument and she throws them in your face, hitting below the belt. Everything you told her about being called stupid in school because you could not read, it comes back out when you get mad. And now you are sitting there saying, I am never telling anybody anything.
When women get mad, the gloves are off; there is a whole song about busting the windows out your car. Do not teach her things about you that she can use against you.

Turn away thine eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another's beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman. Just like it said in 1 Esdras 4: many have erred behind a woman. Do not be lustful after her because she looks good, because things start going into your mind.

There are women that are fine, with the body, all dainty, and blessed with a full-fledged demon. Be careful with that. The Bible is telling you to beware; the Lord is saying, I know what I created, and I know what is powerful. Some of you brothers are weak; do not be deceived by it.

Turn away thine eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another's beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire. You can be destroyed by continuing to stare.
